claims.text: Machine-learning-based process-parameter optimization can reduce residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
Machine-learning-based process-parameter optimization can improve the mechanical properties of additively manufactured miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed intervention is applicable to powder bed fusion or laser powder bed fusion.
Machine learning can optimize process parameters including laser power and scan speed for AlCrFeNiSi additive manufacturing.
Optimization of laser power and scan speed can control the microstructure of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Control of process parameters and microstructure can reduce residual thermal stresses.
Reduced residual thermal stresses will lead to improved mechanical properties.
Machine-learning-optimized components will have lower residual thermal stresses than components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
Machine-learning-optimized components will have better mechanical properties than components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
The intervention is applicable to miniature components with complex geometries.
The effectiveness of machine-learning optimization may depend on the quality of its training data.
The effectiveness of machine-learning optimization may depend on the complexity of process–microstructure–property relationships.
